time_plan.30m: Check whether Fed funds futures / SOFR curve show a parallel dovish shift or if it's isolated to this thin Polymarket strike.

predictions.reasoning: An 11-cut (275bps) scenario for 2026 is an extreme-dovish/recession tail. If implied odds of this many cuts spiked, it would signal expectations of aggressive Fed easing, possibly via emergency cuts amid a crisis. That would compress front-end yields and pull long-end yields lower, lifting long-duration Treasury prices. But 11 cuts is a near-zero base-rate outcome, so any probability move on this specific strike is more likely noise than a genuine macro signal, hence low confidence and a sub-tradable magnitude.

predictions.reasoning: A surge in odds of many Fed cuts implies lower real rates and a weaker dollar, both supportive of gold. An extreme 11-cut scenario would also imply crisis/recession conditions that boost safe-haven demand. However, the strike is an implausible tail and the topic tag ('military_conflict') is likely mislabeled, so the causal chain to gold is speculative and weak; magnitude well below the 700bps tradable threshold.

evidence_used: Market question implies an extreme 275bps (11x25bps) of 2026 Fed easing, including emergency cuts
Resolution tied to official FOMC statements and target-rate changes
Standard macro linkage: more Fed cuts => lower yields, weaker USD, higher gold and bond prices
Note that the 'military_conflict' topic tag appears inconsistent with a Fed-cuts question
uncertainty_notes: 11 cuts is a near-zero base-rate outcome; probability moves on this strike are dominated by noise/liquidity in a thin market
No headline or catalyst provided, so directionality of any implied-probability move is unknown
A 700bps 12h move in liquid ETFs from a rate-expectations shift is implausible absent a crisis; predictions are flagged sub-tradable
The topic tag mismatch reduces confidence that this signal is meaningful

llm_justification.summary: This market prices an implausibly dovish tail — 11 Fed rate cuts (275bps) in 2026, including emergency cuts. If its implied odds spiked, the cleanest read is expectations of aggressive easing/recession, which maps to lower yields (TLT up), a weaker dollar, and higher gold (GLD up). But the strike is an extreme tail dominated by market noise, and the mapping is weak: expected moves are small, confidence is low, and neither prediction meets the 700bps tradable threshold. Treat as a noisy sensor requiring corroboration from the actual rates curve and a real macro catalyst.
key_assumptions: A rise in implied cut-count odds reflects genuine dovish/recession expectations rather than thin-market noise
Standard easing transmission: lower policy-rate path lifts bond and gold prices, weakens USD
No offsetting inflation-shock interpretation that would reverse the bond-positive read
failure_modes: The probability move is illiquid-market noise with no real information content
Aggressive-cut pricing coincides with a growth/inflation scare that hurts long bonds via term-premium repricing
The move was already reflected in the SOFR/fed-funds curve, so ETFs don't react
Proxies (TLT, GLD) are driven by unrelated global flows over the 12h window, swamping any rate-expectation signal
Direction could be reversed if the spike is toward 'No' resolution (fewer cuts), implying hawkish repricing
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
